Scansion of 877 by hand: syllables πρόσ-θεν | Μη-ρι-ο | να-ο-πα | γη-πο-δός | αὐ-τὰρ-ἣ | ὄρ-νις = 16 syllables, four dactyls and two spondees. Two licences are needed and both are real: the να of Μηριόναο must count long (metrical lengthening; the alternative, reading ναο as one syllable, then needs the α of πάγη long), and ἣ must be short before ὄρνις (correption). The scanner’s UNRESOLVED flag is therefore a true irregularity, not a scanner failure; the feminine caesura after the third foot (Μηριόνα|ο) agrees with the scanner. Nothing else in the part is flagged.

## Rulings on the drafter’s doubts

(a) ἀπειλέω “promise” at 863 and 872 against the table’s “threaten” (1.319, 1.388, 21.161, 23.184): ACCEPTED. In both places the verb takes a god in the dative and a future infinitive of sacrifice, with the negative at 863 contrasting with the vow at 872; “threaten” would have Teucer threatening Apollo with a hecatomb. The departure is recorded in new-renderings.md and the 863 note says so and points to 872. Also checked: the 872 note’s “almost word for word” is true (873 = 864 exactly; 872 differs only in the dative).

(b) Quotation marks round Achilles’ rule at 855b–858: KEPT. ἀνώγει at 854 introduces it, and φερέσθω (a third-person imperative) and the future οἴσεται are in the speaker’s voice, not the narrator’s. The speech opens mid-line on its own unit (mark on 855) and closes on the unit ending at 858 (” in both layers). The note’s reason was corrected (see table).

(c) Subject of ἴθυνεν at 871: ACCEPTED WITH A HEDGE. The sense is that Meriones had held a ready arrow for some time while the other man was taking aim, and Teucer is the only other archer present; the l keeps “he” and the i says Teucer. The other reading (Meriones as subject) is not excluded by the Greek, so the note now says “natural reading”. The i was not changed.

(d) Lexical claims in notes: χράομαι (Ionic χρεώμενος, “using it”): sound; Ionic χρέομαι for χράομαι is standard, and the table rejects “needing”. ἰόεις “violet-coloured, dark” from ἴον, with ἰός “rust” noted as the alternative: sound, and the note already says the sense is not known. ἐνδίνων “a rare word”: sound (the form is found only here in Homer’s text). Dual ὥ at 802: sound, ὥ is the dual relative, and ἀρίστω, ἑσσαμένω, ἑλόντε, ἀμφοτέρω, μεμαῶτε, δερκομένω, συνίτην are all dual forms as claimed. Eetion: sound (see above). Asteropaeus: sound (Paeonian leader, killed by Achilles at the river in book 21; 21.179 has ἀπηύρα). Epeius: sound (23.689 ἐπὶ δ’ ὄρνυτο δῖος Ἐπειός, the boxing). Also verified: Leonteus ὄζος Ἄρηος at 2.745; μέγα σθένος for Idomeneus at 13.248; Πριάμοιο βίην at 3.105; κρατερὸν μένος at 10.479; κλήρους … ἑλόντες at 3.316; 753 as the runners’ call; Od. 12.63 τρήρωνες.

(e) κελεύομεν at 802, “we bid” in l and “we call on” in i: ACCEPTED. The table gives κελεύω “bid, order”, and the same Greek line stands in iliad-149 (658) with exactly these words. ἐκέλευσαν at 823 “gave orders” follows the table; ἀνώγει at 854 “bade” and κέλομαι at 894 “urge” also follow it.

(f) ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ at 880–881: ACCEPTED WITH A HEDGE. The bird is feminine, so αὐτῆς would be her; the nearest thing she could fall away from is the mast, and the English says so. The note now gives the reason and says “most naturally”.

(g) ὅ γε ἥρως at 896: ACCEPTED. Agamemnon gave the spear (δῶκε), and ὅ γε “he for his part” resumes the same subject in contrast to what he did with the other prize. The alternative, Meriones (called ἥρως at 893), would have Meriones handing Agamemnon’s cauldron to a herald, which the story does not support. The note names the person, as the table row requires.

## Findings considered and refused

- 802 ὥ περ ἀρίστω: l and i do not render περ (“the very best”). Refused: the published l and i of the same line (iliad-149) omit it, and the repeated line should read alike.
- 805 i “thrust at” for ὀρεξάμενος (l “reaching out to”). Refused: ὀρέγομαι is used of a weapon reaching out, and “thrust at” is the idiomatic English; the note says the weapon is understood.
- 876 i “stuck in the earth” for πάγη ἐπὶ γαίῃ (“on the earth”). Refused: the arrow that has come down and “stuck” is in the ground; l keeps “on”.
- 857 i drops γάρ in “being the lesser”. Refused: the participle carries the reason.
- 894 i drops γάρ in “I for my part urge it”. Refused: the clause follows a semicolon and still reads as the reason; the l has “for”.
- 896 i “the hero himself” for ὅ γε. Refused: acceptable English for the contrastive ὅ γε; l has “but he, the hero”.
- 862 i “drew the first turn” (object not in the Greek). Refused: the note says so and says the next unit confirms it.
- 826 σόλος “lump”, 885 ἀνθεμόεντα l “flowery” / i “decorated with flowers”, 850 ἰόεντα “dark”, 851 ἡμιπέλεκκα “half-axe”: all follow the new-renderings rows with their reasons; no objection.
- 830, 801, 825, 813, 811, 831, 864, 873, 895 (repeats): l and i of the whole-unit repeats match the published ones exactly (801 and 830 against iliad-145/147/149/150; the rest differ only in unit shape, and the partial repeats keep the published wording as far as the sentence allows). 895 i names Achilles (“So Achilles spoke”) where the published unit says Nestor; the context requires it and the unit is not a whole-unit repeat.
- Remembered English: nothing found that arrived fully formed; the stock phrases (“skin-cutting”, “long-shadowed”, “hollow ships”, “timorous dove”, “scion of Ares”) are the table’s or the drafter’s rows.
- Positional claims (“begins/ends in the middle of line N” at 815, 834, 853, 854, 855, 862, 869, 871, 877, 881, 886, 896, and the cross-references to 798–800, 807–808, 843, 845, 851, 860, 884, 885) were each checked against the unit’s `t` and the source line: all true.

# Pass 2 — gloss.json (67 novel forms, 20 __broaden__ entries as delivered)

Method: every novel parse checked against the line in the revised units.json; every __broaden__ base compared character by character with the current root iliad-glossary.json entry (all 20 delivered bases equal the root text exactly; the new reading is joined with " · " in each); every entry checked for length under 230 characters, typographic ’ only, no line numbers, no "here" (the only hits were "there" inside φθῇσιν, a false alarm; the single real "here" was in κῦρε). The key set equals novel-forms.json exactly (67). No entry assumes the old "amazed" reading of θάμβησαν: θάμβησάν and θηεῦντό are known forms whose root entries ("be struck with wonder", "gaze at, watch in wonder") already match the revised 881; the only nearby entry, the ἔχε broaden, quoted "amazement gripped them all" and now reads "wonder held them all".

Counts: 1 medium-high (wrong governing word), 5 medium, 10 low; 1 broaden refused and deleted; 1 broaden added.

## The glosser’s flagged forms

- φερέσθων: "pres. imper. 3 pl. (or dual) mid." is correct and agrees with the revised unit note; kept.
- ποδός broaden: bases agree with root; both new readings are true of the line (δῆσεν ποδός; πρόσθεν … ποδός); kept, split.
- χρεώμενος: "χράομαι — use; pres. part. mid. dep., epic uncontracted (= Attic χρώμενος)" correct and matches the unit note and the table (needing rejected); kept. The "+ dat." is the verb’s general construction.
- ἰόεντα, αὐτοχόωνον: corrected as above.
- ἐνδίνων: "ἔνδινα — entrails, innards (plural only; origin uncertain)": correct (the word is found once, in this line); kept.
- ἥμασιν / ἥμονες lemmas: ἧμα (throw, from ἵημι) with "in throws", and ἥμων (thrower) in the plural, are the standard lemmas and agree with the units; kept.
- αὐτοῦ broaden: the new reading (ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ, "from it", masculine thing, the mast) is true and agrees with the revised note at 880; it partly overlaps the earlier "masc. gen. sg. standing for a masculine thing" reading but adds the preposition and is not wrong; kept.
- καλαύροπα gender: feminine is right (the relative ἣ in the next line agrees with it); kept.
- κῦρε: corrected as above.

## Considered and refused

- ἀπόπροθι, πίονες, ἀγροί, ὁππότερός, ἀτεμβόμενός, ἐξείρυσε, ἐφεζομένη, λίασθεν, πτάτο, μέγηρε, λάχεν: parses true of the line; no change. (ἐξείρυσε "with the lengthened εἰρ- of ἐρύω" left as is: the form is the augmented aorist of the lengthened stem.)
- The glosser’s Teucer and Polypoetes entries mention other persons (half-brother of Ajax, son of Peirithous): true of the poem and not pinned to a line; kept.
- Known forms spot-checked for coverage (ἣ, ἂν, ὥ, ἀρίστω, ἔπλευ, ἴδμεν, ἀφέηκε, ἀνώγει, ἑξείης, ἔρυτο, πάγη, τάμε, ὑπὸ + gen., ἱστὸν, ἔπι, ἑλισσομένη and others): all covered by the root entries; only πάλαι needed a broaden.
- Not rechecked: whether the build’s merge (the "__broaden__" mechanism) accepts the replaced ἀγῶνα omission; nothing depends on it.
